summary: CI: the Review checks finish sooner and use fewer runner-seconds, with every check still running. Two runs of the final workflow took 175 s and 173 s from the first job's start to the last job's end (2 s queue each) and used 2215 and 2202 runner-seconds, against 252 to 341 s and 2668 to 3016 runner-seconds for three runs of the previous layout (41287595577, 41303275962, 41319698135). A new push to a pull request cancels its run still in progress (one concurrency group per pull request, or per ref for merge queue runs). One Production build job runs npm run build, which type-checks every project, bundles and checks the documentation and third-party sources; the browser and Firefox jobs no longer repeat it. They run the new npm run build:bundle, the same dist without the type check, while Playwright installs the browser and its system packages in the background. The browser is cached per Playwright version, and the Chromium jobs install only the headless shell. Unit tests run in four shards instead of two, split by measured file time instead of by path hash: a Vitest sequencer in scripts/unit-test-shards.ts reads scripts/unit-test-shard-weights.json and only applies with --shard. Each file is still in exactly one shard, and within a shard the files keep Vitest's project order (jsdom and kernel suites before the pure-domain timing checks), heaviest first. Each unit shard keeps its JSON timing report as an artifact for seven days, and scripts/update-unit-test-shard-weights.ts rebuilds the table from them. Browser journeys run in eleven shards instead of twelve, sized by PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS fitted to measured run times; shard 10 ends with the large indexeddb-workbench job, as shard 11 of 12 did, so it finishes with the other worker idle. A run has 20 runnable jobs plus verify, under the free plan's 20 concurrent jobs. Test changes: the precision-literal and feature-activity repository scans get a 30 s timeout instead of Vitest's 5 s default, with the same assertions; cad-sketch-point-on-line presses the V axis by its button role and checks it is selected, because the released bore drag locks the canvas until the draft takes its edit and an earlier press could be dropped; 13 unit tests cover the shard split and the weight table.
warning: Not breaking. CI and test configuration only: no app code, schema, output, storage or agent tool change. Check names change: Production build and browser journeys (n/12) becomes Production build plus Browser journeys (n/11), and Unit tests (n/2) becomes (n/4); main has no required-check list naming them. A stale weight table or browser weight list only makes shards less even, because every file and journey still runs exactly once. The browser weights use Playwright's PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS variable; if a later Playwright stops reading it, the shards fall back to equal journey counts and still run every journey. Browser journeys now run against a bundle that was not type-checked in the same job; the Production build job type-checks the same commit and verify requires it.

checklist.schema: No schema change. UPID, post schema, engine API, CAD document and save envelope are unchanged.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change in the app.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. WebMCP tools, their arguments, results and discovery are unchanged.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. The post conformance and machine package validation steps still run in the contracts job.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Nothing is migrated or rewritten.
checklist.verification: Runs 41336953121 (bdbbe67f) and 41338035411 (86af1464) of the final workflow passed every job except Contracts and release record. That job passed lint, ui:check and icons:check and failed at the release check only because this record's previous version 0.0.799 is not yet on main, so its post docs, post conformance and machine package steps were skipped there; they pass locally on this branch. Each run executed 631 unit test files with 7307 tests (main's 630 files and 7294 tests in run 41319698135 of the merged main tree, plus the new shard test file's 13), 235 Chromium journeys with 2 skipped, and 8 Firefox journeys with 1 skipped, the same journeys as main. In 41336953121 cad-sketch-point-on-line passed on its retry, which led to the spec fix; 41338035411 retried nothing. The critical path was the slowest unit shard, 169 s in both; the slowest browser shard took 149 s and 155 s. In run 41319698135 Unit tests (2/2) took 336 s, and each browser shard spent 35 to 56 s building and 16 to 135 s installing Chromium; in the final runs the bundle and install together took 11 to 23 s per browser job. Locally: npm run build, npm run lint, npm run ui:check, npm run icons:check, npm run post:docs:check, the post conformance and machine package validation of the Robofil 100 v2 fixtures, the shard tests, and cad-sketch-point-on-line three times. With the sketch solver's replies delayed by 800 ms after the drag, the previous spec failed twice at the same step as on CI and the updated one passed twice.

publicNotes.summary: Internal change to the automated review checks; the app is unchanged.
changes: The automated checks on proposed changes finish sooner, use less total runner time and stop early when a newer change replaces them, with no visible change in the app.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, controller output, CAD files and agent tools are unchanged.
